clue.text: Most nasty blokes circling area in front of estate

indicators.note: the enclosed group comes before the estate abbreviation in the answer
the blokes go round the area letter, enclosing it

parts.note: blokes are men
EST is a common abbreviation for estate

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant men are hanging around outside a property, looking threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative: the most nasty person is the most spiteful, a sense of mean in British usage.

clue.text: Reason I vote differently after Macron's summit

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the top letter in the answer
the summit of a word in a down clue is its top, first letter
differently means the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A French voter explains a changed ballot after the president's summit meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason for doing something.

clue.text: Sailor with paddle departs on a boat?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
an oar is a paddle
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a paddle and leaves aboard a small craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship or other vessel is the meaning; the question mark marks the definition as a phrase.

clue.text: Fan his aunt set spinning

indicators.note: spinning suggests the letters whirl round into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An admirer's aunt has been set twirling, perhaps on a dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a keen devotee, a passionate admirer of something.

clue.text: Spells words

definitions.meaning: periods of time, as in ... of office or school ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: periods such as school sessions, and expressions used for things.

clue.text: Notable person from Belgrade cut debts?

explanation.surface: Someone from Serbia seems to have had their debts written off, perhaps a newsworthy event.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable deserves attention; a serious matter is significant and weighty, a near synonym.

clue.text: Catches up with a chapter on American slave

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: traps are catches, snares

explanation.surface: Someone captures an American slave, bringing a chapter of history to light.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator who led a great revolt against Rome was a slave.

clue.text: Weak female leaves bar

indicators.note: leaves means the female letter goes out of the word

parts.note: frail means weak

explanation.surface: A feeble woman walks out of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the pub she leaves, but it is the definition: a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a long rod or bar, as in a towel rail.

clue.text: Completely incorrect? Correct!

parts.note: out means wrong, as a guess may be out
right means correct

explanation.surface: A teacher's marking: totally wrong, then on reflection, right!
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly, entirely, as in rejected outright.

clue.text: Smooth-tongued learner ignored head's complaint

indicators.note: ignored means the learner letter is left out of the word

parts.note: slick means glib, smooth-tongued
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: A glib student overlooks the headteacher's grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in medical usage is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Hawk grabbing river fish

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them, sell them pushily

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird, but here it is the verb meaning to peddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a well-known freshwater game fish, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Authentic old Spanish coin — is it brought back with cents?

parts.note: the real was an old silver coin of Spain

indicators.note: brought back means the word it is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cent or cents

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an old Spanish coin, returned with some small change, is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic and lifelike both describe something true to reality, so they are synonyms here.

clue.text: New Tory visit embraces upper-class flair

new suggests the letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosity is great technical skill, a brilliant talent close in sense to flair.

clue.text: Mark slinging every other character out

indicators.note: every second letter is thrown out, leaving the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Someone throwing out alternate letters while leaving a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a symbol or trace, the same thing as a mark.

clue.text: Telephone some hotel instead of small caravan

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile telephone

indicators.note: instead of says the hotel letter replaces the small letter in the word some

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Phoning a hotel rather than booking a cramped caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small caravan' reads as one phrase, but 'small' is S, swapped out of SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A static caravan in which people live is the same thing as a trailer home.

clue.text: Wife leaving when cot light's off? Sleeper may want these on

leaving says the wife letter departs from the word when

explanation.walkthrough: Removing W from WHEN leaves HEN; 'off' then rearranges HEN, COT and LIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are worn by people in bed, so a sleeper dresses in them.

clue.text: The man on craft considered sincere

art is a craft, a skill
felt means considered, believed

clue.text: English Signal Officer initially concealing urge for drink

initially means take the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: to press is to urge

explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee is a drink.

clue.text: Adult ordered a claret according to individually priced menu

clue.text: Spies man with lash developing flogging skill

explanation.surface: Spies hold a man and a whip, evolving a talent for beating.

explanation.definitionFit: Flogging is British slang for selling, and the art of persuading buyers is exactly that skill.

clue.text: Insect — chap's holding it up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads upwards, backwards

explanation.definitionFit: A praying mantis is a predatory insect.

clue.text: Tense mistake creating fear

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

clue.text: Rally vehicle going west then east

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A rally car drives one way, then turns back the other way.

clue.text: Steady partner for person in the same club

parts.note: steady means stable, firm
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A dependable companion is sought for a fellow member of the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague from the same organisation, team or yard is called this; originally horses from one stable.

clue.text: One left enthralled by friend's physique

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend, buddy

clue.text: Spain callously captures member of ancient empire

indicators.note: captures says the two words hold the letters inside them, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Spain brutally seizes a subject of a fallen empire, recalling the conquistadors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peruvian empire conquered by the Spanish was that of this people.

clue.text: African plain almost peaceful — get idealistic at first

parts.note: serene means peaceful

clue.text: Scoundrel taking head off freshwater mammal

clue.text: Evident eating a cold ham might do this

C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is plainly seen eating a slice of cold ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat but is a bad, showy actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor exaggerates, performing with too much emphasis on stage.

clue.text: One puts gear on sideboard

a kitchen cabinet with shelves for plates, a Welsh one being typical
